newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse lifts Sanevit suspension.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse lifts Sanevit suspension.

text.p: The Bucharest bourse said on Tuesday listed Sanevit SA syringe maker, suspended from trading last November, had been readmitted to the market after an announcement on its latest shareholders' meeting.
Sanevit had the statement published in two newspapers, in line with bourse rules, the stock exchange said.
The statement reported Sanevit's activity in 1996, when its total revenues amounted to a preliminary 15.9 billion lei, with total spending at 14.8 billion lei.
The company said final 1996 financial results would be made available at a later date.
It also said shareholders had approved a 1997 investment plan and amended the composition of the auditing commission.
A decision on adding imported equipment to Sanevit's capital base of 24.7 billion lei has yet to be approved by a general meeting of shareholders, the statement said.

Sanevit, Romania's sole producer of disposable syringes, bought equipment from Italy's Penta Group on a $37 million credit guaranteed by the Romanian state. The equipment was assessed by accountants Coopers and Lybrand, but the results of the assessment are still unavailable.
"When they have recalculated their new capital they will issue another statement," exchange general manager Stere Farmache said.

The company entered Romania's capital market when the Bucharest bourse opened in November 1995. It dominated trading for several months as the exchange's sole private stock, but then it fell sharply throughout 1996.
Before suspension, Sanevit closed at 9,100 lei, compared with a 71,000 lei closing peak in November 1995. ($=7,024 lei)
